title: Accession manuscript: September15 primary-record follow-up
scope: Additional reads and final-body inspection; prior foundational facsimile, participant and archive audits remain separately cited. Some public sources were already identified or partly read in the earlier dossier; this is not five new independent discoveries.

sources.title: Clinton–Zhu joint press conference, April 8, 1999
sources.read_scope: Selected complete WTO exchanges: opening remarks through Zhu’s political-atmosphere explanation; Clinton’s case for engagement and Zhu’s concessions/reform/gift reply. Surrounding questions inspected; whole press conference not claimed as a topical audit.
sources.evidentiary_use: Public disagreement over why closure failed; Zhu’s stated reform rationale and refusal of gift framing.
sources.limits: US record of interpreted Chinese remarks; not independently checked against a Chinese transcript; economic statistics and unrelated accusations not verified.

sources.title: Sandy Berger press briefing, Ankara, November 15, 1999
sources.read_scope: All WTO questions and answers read, including the April comparison, Chinese gains, broader relationship, PNTR and congressional authority, and Seattle observer question. Other foreign-policy exchanges not audited.
sources.evidentiary_use: US public defense of the agreement and distinct domestic/multilateral steps.
sources.limits: Contemporary public advocacy, not full final annexes or evidence of the distribution of concessions.

sources.title: Summary of US–China Bilateral WTO Agreement, November 16, 1999
sources.read_scope: Complete substantive HTML, Agriculture through Textiles, including every sector and trade-remedy section.
sources.evidentiary_use: A contemporary US-reported outcome column for four issue comparisons; 12-year safeguard and 15-year antidumping description; sector-specific equity/timing.
sources.limits: Unilateral public summary, not authenticated bilateral annexes. Its legal characterizations are not adopted as a determination of the later WTO protocol’s interpretation.

sources.title: WTO Press/148, Moore welcomes US–China deal but cautions more work remains, November 15, 1999
sources.read_scope: Complete substantive release including final Working Party, preparatory work and Seattle paragraphs.
sources.evidentiary_use: Institutional distinction between bilateral deal, remaining accessions work, and observer status.
sources.limits: A contemporary description of the institution’s next stages, not a private negotiating record.

sources.title: 中华人民共和国与美国市场准入协议 / Agreement on Market Access between the PRC and the USA, November 15, 1999
sources.source_type: signed bilateral agreement bodies, Chinese and English, in later official documentary collection
sources.read_scope: Both complete signed body pages, printed1095–1096/PDF1102–1103, visually read. Adjacent contents and next-item heading checked. Annexes1–4 not reproduced with these pages and remain unacquired as this instrument’s annexes.
sources.evidentiary_use: Agreed status vs Nov12 conditional proposal; Annexes1–3 goods/agriculture/services and Annex4 rules on access to each other’s markets; joint notification and transmission to WTO for incorporation into multilateral accession negotiations.
sources.limits: Paired language bodies are versions of one source, not independent corroboration. They do not reveal all detailed final concessions, Chinese or US internal approval sequences, or actual performance.
sources.relationship_to_prior_record: Additional reading within CN-WTO-B3; earlier audits covered the April MOU and November offers, not these two signed final bodies.

new_documentary_findings: Both final signed language bodies distinguish agreement from later incorporation into multilateral accession negotiations.
Four-issue comparison now includes a complete contemporaneous US public summary but still does not claim acquisition of the bilateral annexes.
remaining_documents: April8 US statement attachments in authenticated exchanged versions
April NEC–NSC decision memorandum and relevant Chinese instructions
Final multilateral schedules must be kept distinct from the US bilateral snapshot.
independent_review: Editorial agent reviewed the introduction and is reviewing the accession draft; this record does not claim independent rereading of every prior source.
